pattern: Stateful real-time collaboration: route every participant of one object to a single owner (lease), let the owner order and transform concurrent operations, append each op to a log before acknowledging, snapshot asynchronously for fast loads, and keep ephemeral state (presence) in memory only.

tips.nudge: What makes this different from a plain text editor that saves to the cloud?
tips.hint: Write a functional requirement about several people editing the same document at once.
tips.show: F1: Several users edit the same document concurrently; everyone converges to the same text.

tips.nudge: How quickly should a co-author see your keystroke, and should your own typing ever wait?
tips.hint: State a latency target for edits reaching others.
tips.show: N1: Others see an edit within ~200 ms p99 in-region; local typing never waits on the network.

checks.label: Past states of a document covered

tips.nudge: Someone deleted half the document by mistake an hour ago. Then what?
tips.hint: Add a requirement about seeing and restoring earlier states.
tips.show: F3: Version history: browse and restore earlier revisions.

tips.nudge: The server said 'saved'. What must never happen next?
tips.hint: Add a non-functional requirement about losing edits.
tips.show: N3: Durability: an acknowledged edit is never lost.

tips.nudge: How many people are typing at the same moment, and how often does each one send?
tips.hint: ops/s = concurrent typists × batched ops per second each.
tips.show: ops_per_sec = 5M typists × ~1 batch/s ≈ 5M ops/s (but only ~500 ops/s on the busiest single doc).

tips.nudge: Every open editor tab keeps a channel open. How many at peak?
tips.hint: Count connected users at peak (editors and viewers).
tips.show: concurrent_connections ≈ 20M at peak.

checks.label: Fleet size for live sessions estimated

tips.nudge: One server can hold how many open sockets?
tips.hint: servers = connections / sockets per server (~50k).
tips.show: collab_servers = 20M / 50k ≈ 400.

tips.nudge: If you keep every edit, how much does that add per day?
tips.hint: log growth = ops/s × bytes per op × seconds per day.
tips.show: oplog_per_day = 5M × 100 B × 86,400 ≈ 43 TB/day (snapshots + compaction of old ops keep it bounded).

tips.nudge: What does the editor download when a tab opens?
tips.hint: A GET that returns the document state and the revision it corresponds to.
tips.show: GET /docs/{id} → {snapshot, rev, acl}

tips.nudge: After opening, how do edits flow both ways?
tips.hint: Define the persistent channel and the messages on it, including the revision each edit was based on.
tips.show: WS /docs/{id}/session: client → {op, base_rev, client_seq}; server → {ack rev} | {op, rev, author} | {presence}.

tips.nudge: What exactly do you store for one keystroke batch?
tips.hint: A record per edit: which document, its position in the order, what changed, who.
tips.show: op_log(doc_id, rev, op, author, client_seq, ts) + snapshots(doc_id, rev, state).

checks.label: Live connection and routing designed as their own part

tips.nudge: Edits must reach co-authors in ~200 ms. Which channel, and which server do all editors of one document talk to?
tips.hint: Add a part for the session: compare polling, SSE, WebSockets and P2P, and decide how a document maps to a server.
tips.show: Part 'Real-time session': WebSocket per editor, routed by doc_id to a collaboration server holding the doc's ownership lease (etcd).

checks.label: Merging simultaneous edits designed as its own part

tips.nudge: Alice inserts at position 10 while Bob deletes position 5. Apply both naively and what happens?
tips.hint: Add a part for concurrency control: compare locking, last-write-wins, Operational Transformation and CRDTs.
tips.show: Part 'Concurrency control': OT with the doc's owner assigning revisions and transforming each op against the ops its sender hadn't seen; CRDT if offline-first were required.

checks.label: Saving edits and history designed as its own part

tips.nudge: Saving the whole 50 KB document on every keystroke: what does that cost at your op rate?
tips.hint: Add a part for persistence: compare full saves, a pure op log and an op log with snapshots.
tips.show: Part 'Persistence': append each op to an op log (doc_id, rev) before acking; snapshot every ~500 ops asynchronously.

checks.label: Showing collaborators designed as its own part

tips.nudge: Cursor moves happen far more often than edits. Should they be stored?
tips.hint: Add a part for presence: compare persisting it, a shared pub/sub and in-memory soft state.
tips.show: Part 'Presence': ephemeral in the owner server's memory, broadcast at ≤ 10 Hz on the same socket, cursors transformed like ops.

tips.nudge: 20M sockets across hundreds of servers. Who decides where each one goes?
tips.hint: Something in front that spreads connections and keeps a document's editors together.
tips.show: L7 load balancer that terminates WebSockets and routes by doc_id (consistent hashing) to the owner.

checks.label: A stateful place where a document's edits meet

tips.nudge: Where is the single order of a document's edits decided?
tips.hint: Add a stateful service that holds open documents and their editors.
tips.show: Collaboration server ×N: each owns a set of documents (lease), runs OT and broadcasts.

checks.label: Fast document open despite long histories

tips.nudge: A document with a million edits: does opening it replay all of them?
tips.hint: Store periodic materialised states somewhere.
tips.show: Snapshot store (object storage) with the document state every ~500 ops.

checks.label: Edits recorded before they are confirmed

tips.nudge: When may the server tell a client 'your edit is saved'?
tips.hint: Connect the collaboration service to an append-only record of edits.
tips.show: Collaboration server → op log (append op @ rev before ack) and → op stream for snapshotting.

checks.label: Losing the server that owns a document handled

tips.nudge: The server holding a busy document crashes. Who takes over, and what about edits in flight?
tips.hint: Compare a hot standby with rebuilding from storage, and say how you prevent two owners.
tips.show: Lease expires (~5 s); a new owner loads snapshot + op-log tail; clients reconnect with their last acked rev; a fencing token stops the old owner writing.

tips.nudge: A laptop loses Wi-Fi for 10 minutes while its user keeps typing. What happens on reconnect?
tips.hint: Think about what the client keeps, what it asks for, and how its edits fit in.
tips.show: Client keeps pending ops + last acked rev; server sends ops since that rev; client transforms pending ops and resends (idempotent by client_seq).

tips.nudge: A company all-hands doc has 5,000 viewers. What breaks?
tips.hint: Think about one owner per document and how far that stretches.
tips.show: Viewers move to read-only fan-out replicas fed by the op stream; more collab servers via consistent hashing on doc_id; op log partitions by doc_id.
